title: Remembers what you told it, and gets out of your way
highlights: Grok Voice 3.0: talk with your bots live, interrupt any time, and they do the work while you talk
Undo what a task did to your files: one button on the answer, or just say "undo that"
Dry run any routine: it reads for real and lists what it would send or change, without doing it
Bots remember what you already told them: "email my landlord", "the usual", "near my place" just work, without repeating yourself
Before asking you something you already told it, a bot checks its memory and your other chats first
Talking to a bot is one ongoing conversation, like Grok Bot: no new chat in Recents each time
A bot's chat shows just the conversation: "On it.", then "<name> is working…", then the answer
Settings are the basics only: about 8 per page, no Advanced sections, no look or approval rules to manage
If a step takes over a minute, the bot tells you in plain words instead of sitting silently

sections.title: Grok Voice 3.0
items: With Grok as your voice and an xAI key saved, a voice conversation is live: Grok listens, answers in its own voice, and stops the moment you talk over it
For anything real (your memory, files, apps, email, the web, an action) it hands the request to the bot, which does it in its chat, and Grok tells you the result
About $0.08 a minute, counted against your monthly limit; if Grok can't connect, the standard voice takes over

sections.title: Safer, clearer
items: Undo puts back files a task changed and takes away files it made (kept in a holding folder, never deleted); a file you changed since is left alone
Dry run, next to Test on a routine: reads your email, calendar and pages for real, and only lists what it would send, write or post
Start a fresh conversation with any bot from its profile; it still remembers everything, and earlier conversations are under Past conversations
A bot's profile shows what it cost this month
Bot chats show system lines again ("Paused routine", undo, messages between bots); only status chatter is hidden

sections.title: Memory
items: Bots match what you said by meaning, not just the same words: "my boss" finds your manager, the weather knows your city, and a food question always brings in your allergies and diet
Bigger models see more of what you told them (up to about 4,000 tokens of memories on a 1M-token model), only what bears on the request
A long chat brings back a detail you gave early on, word for word, even after it was summarized
One memory vault for every bot, always remembering the most; there's no per-bot vault or "how much to remember" to set
Generic questions ("what is an IP address?") don't pull your personal details in

sections.title: Simpler
items: The home screen is a greeting and the message box, nothing else
The sidebar: search and new chat at the top, your bots with bigger icons and their last message, Recents only for chats you start; Library and Memory are in your profile menu
A bot's profile: its routines, Permissions (Ask or Auto) and Customize. Notifications are automatic; the morning check-in, vault and "runs on <model>" are gone (ask the bot in chat instead)
Routines are made, changed and removed by asking the bot; there's no New routine form
Setup no longer asks about voice or the microphone: your voice is Grok if you added a Grok key, otherwise ChatGPT
The message box is just the box: no folder chip until a chat works in a folder, no model picker (Auto picks), and the "Enter / ⌘Enter" tip only the first time
The chat header only shows the browser and side panel buttons when there's something in them, and a bot's chat ends on its answer

sections.title: Smarter and steadier
items: A quick math question while a bot works ("18% of $1,740?") is answered instantly; other side questions use a faster model
A double-check that finds and fixes a mistake keeps the fix, even when it takes longer than a minute and a half
A new script is the simplest one that works, tested once on a sample, with copy-paste steps to run it

title: A simpler SahilBot: every button has one job
highlights: Ask a quick question while a bot works on something long and it answers right away; the long job keeps going
Notes are the bots' own memory, with no screen to manage: ask a bot to forget something or export your notes
Permissions and setup stick: updates no longer make you grant permissions or go through setup again
Your main bot is a "New bot" you can rename just by asking, and pinned bots are big avatars at the top of the sidebar
Voice is one choice, Grok first, ChatGPT or Claude, and typed replies are never read aloud on their own
New bot asks for just a name, an icon and a color: the bot works out its job with you in its first chat, starting from its name
Settings has six clear sections, each with a one-line explanation, and no "More settings" menus
The voice bar is calmer: a smooth wave that follows your voice, one line of status, and plain words with a "Set up voice" button when voice isn't ready
Typing "stop", "cancel" or "never mind" while a bot works really stops it, like the Stop button, including its helpers and commands
⌘F finds words in the open chat, ⌘1 to ⌘9 open your bots, and ⌘/ shows every shortcut
Updates and backup sizes show right away instead of making you wait
Smoother animations and easier-to-read chat text

sections.title: Every button has one job
items: There is no Notes screen: notes are the bots' own memory, and Vault only means passwords
Settings is the gear at the bottom of the sidebar; the second gear in the chat header is gone
One "New bot" button when you have no bots yet, instead of two
The chat menu no longer repeats "About": click the bot's name for its settings, routines and files
"Attach a folder's files" (in +) and "Choose folder" (under the box) say what each one does
Needs you is called Needs you everywhere, and Brain is called Brain everywhere
An empty Brain shows one thing to do, Connect apps, instead of a disabled refresh button and zeros
The Help menu is now Keyboard Shortcuts, Connect Apps and Settings
Every page is the same width, and empty pages say one thing to do instead of showing empty tools
"Waiting on you" questions no longer pre-pick an answer you didn't choose
Settings → Connected keeps Cursor, MCP and Shortcuts links under "For developers"
When a bot can't confirm something worked, you see its plain explanation and a small "Needs a check" tag, not a technical report
Make a bot by asking ("make me a Homework Helper bot"): a new bot with its own chat, job, color and emoji icon, in seconds. Delete, hide, pin or rename one by asking too (deleting asks first)
Each bot can have its own emoji icon; its profile has Hide and Delete
The sidebar says Library and Memory, and Needs you shows only when something is waiting
"Show work" on the status line opens the plan, sources and files (it opens by itself the first time); every finished task shows a one-line finish line
Status says file names, not paths ("Creating invoice.pdf in Downloads"); picking anything in the sidebar closes Settings and highlights right away; sending jumps to the newest message

Opening an installed app (Calculator) no longer warns "can't be undone"; looking at running apps or checking a Python version doesn't ask; a reply that needs Accessibility comes with a button that opens it

sections.title: Smarter at real work
items: Make a routine without typing a request: Bot details → Routines → New routine (what, how often, when)
Change a routine by just asking ("move it to 9:10 and add Saturdays"): it's updated in place and keeps its history
A side answer shows the message it answers, so it's clear which question it's replying to
A bot that stalls ("Want me to go ahead?", "On it!" with nothing done) is told to just do what you asked, so you don't have to say "go ahead"
Routines say what is really happening: starting now, running, done (with when it ran) or paused; a one-time reminder runs within 20 seconds of its time
Bots change part of a file without rewriting it (a new edit tool), and a file can no longer be cut short by writing back only the part a bot saw
A server a bot starts ("listening on…") keeps running in the background instead of blocking the chat, so the bot can use it next
An API key a bot reads in a file (like .env) is hidden if it copies it into its reply
A project's own docs/ folder is readable and writable (it used to be mistaken for SahilBot's manual)
"I'll add it now" with nothing done is caught for everyday edits too (add, update, rename, save…), and asks that name a file to write go straight to work
Every task ends: if a bot is only double-checking an answer it already wrote, a new message ends that run with the answer and starts fresh, and a double-check never runs past 90 seconds
Answers never vanish while a bot double-checks them, and the checked answer replaces the draft in one bubble instead of appearing twice
A one-time reminder that fires while its chat is busy waits its turn instead of being dropped
A bot never replaces a file it hasn't opened: it reads it first, saves under a new name (like name-2.py), or asks
Internal markup from some models (":codex-file-citation{…}") never shows in the chat

On your ChatGPT or Grok plan, each chat (and each bot) keeps one ongoing conversation with the model instead of resending the whole chat: less of your plan used, and the model keeps its context and compacts it itself. Cloud models use their full context window (up to 1M) by default
The websites a bot used show under its answer, including pages it read in the built-in browser and answers written when a long task runs out of steps

sections.title: You
items: Settings → You: Send with ⌘↵ (↵ makes a new line) and Check spelling while typing
What bots learn from (sources, pause, recently removed) is in Settings → Memory → What it learns from
Setup asks your first name, then your last name and birthday (optional), ready for signing in with Google later. Settings → You has all three
Bottom left shows your initials and name, like Grok Bot; click it for Settings, right-click for scheduled, usage and more

sections.title: Privacy & safety
items: Mac apps: Allow now asks macOS for real (it's what puts SahilBot in the Automation list), with one button instead of two
Three tabs instead of five: Passwords, Backups and What it may see
Passwords has four tabs instead of eight: Logins (with API keys), Cards, IDs & notes, and Security (with history)

sections.title: Bots and pins
items: Notes are the bots' own memory: there is no Notes screen. Ask a bot to forget something and it removes it; ask for your notes and it exports them to your Downloads folder
The main bot starts as "New bot" (SahilBot is the app). Ask it in chat ("call yourself Juno") and it renames itself; nothing else can rename it
Pinned bots are big avatars at the top of the sidebar again, like Grok Bot: one pin is extra large, several sit in a row
The button for another bot says "Add a bot", so it never looks like a bot named "New bot"

sections.title: Settings
items: Six sections: You, AI & spending, Apps, Memory, Privacy & safety, Voice. Each one says what it's for
Spending sits with the AI settings, and what SahilBot may do on its own sits with privacy
Text size and steps in chats (Summary or Every step) are in the main list; rarely used options are in one Advanced fold at the bottom
"How answers are picked" is a simple choice: Best answers, Balanced or Lowest cost
Spending choices read Monthly limit, No limit and Don't spend

sections.title: Voice
items: One choice: Grok, ChatGPT or Claude (Claude opens its own voice mode). Grok comes first when its key is there
Typed replies are never read aloud on their own: the speaker on a message reads it, and voice conversations talk
Bottom right of the message box, like Grok Bot: dictate in a grey circle, a voice conversation in a solid one
The wave moves smoothly with your voice and SahilBot's, and calms down when nobody is talking
Transcript, voices, speed and language are behind one "⋯" button in the bar
If voice isn't set up, the bar says what to do in one sentence, and the button opens the right setting
The dictate shortcut reads ⌘D everywhere, and the talk and dictate buttons say what each one does

sections.title: Keyboard
items: ⌘B hides or shows the sidebar, ⇧⌘F searches, ⌃Tab goes to the next bot, and View → Reload (⌘R) is always there
⇧⌘I opens the bot's details (routines, library), ⌥↑ / ⌥↓ go to the previous or next bot, ⌘I jumps to the message box
⌘F: every match in the chat is highlighted; Enter and ⇧Enter step through them
⌘1 to ⌘9 open your bots in the order the sidebar lists them
Help → Keyboard Shortcuts (⌘/) shows every shortcut on one page, including your Quick Ask key
In the ⌘K menu, ⌘1 to ⌘9 pick a row instead of switching bots behind it

sections.title: Smoother everywhere
items: Update downloads skip a slow re-check of a file that was already verified, and the sidebar says "Getting the update", then "Restart to update"
Backup sizes are remembered instead of being recounted every time you open Settings
A question with answer choices shows once, on its card, instead of twice
The "working on…" line under a chat names the step running right now, never an old one
Messages fade in, chat text has more space between lines, and hover effects match across the app. Reduced motion is respected

sections.title: Fixes
items: Setup picks up where you left off: granting a permission makes macOS quit and reopen SahilBot, and setup now continues on the same step instead of starting over

Updates keep the permissions you granted (Screen Recording, Accessibility, Automation, Full Disk Access) and Keychain access: releases are signed with SahilBot's own certificate, so macOS sees the same app after every update. The first update to this version asks once more; after that they stay

title: Medical research you can trust, a cleaner look, and keys that stay put
highlights: API keys no longer disappear when macOS Keychain is slow or still locked, and a backup copy of the key brings them back if it's deleted
Medical answers come from PubMed, guidelines and FDA labels, and every cited paper is checked before you see the answer
Everything SahilBot remembers, including your decisions, is now organized in your vault like Obsidian
A copy of everything (data, memories, vault notes and your keys, encrypted) goes to a separate backup folder every day
A cleaner sidebar, home screen and Settings, with fewer buttons
Auto now recognizes medical, travel, business, engineering and coding-agent requests and sends each to the right model and tools
Maps and travel: places, directions, travel times and things to do, with Google Maps links (a Google Maps key is optional)
SahilBot reads its own manual when it isn't sure how to do something, with new pages on business, engineering and coding agents
Bots keep working on their own: no need to say "continue", routines never get skipped, and every bot can read what the others learned
Talk to a bot and it goes off to do the work while you keep talking, then tells you out loud when it's done
Voices are ChatGPT's or Grok's: pick one, its speed and your language right in the voice bar
Click or hold ⌘D to dictate
Decks and documents keep tables, web pictures and charts in every export
The agent catches more false "done" claims and gives up less
The Privacy Gate is out of beta, and your server can use your Mac safely

sections.title: Your keys stay put
items: The real cause of keys vanishing is fixed: when macOS Keychain didn't answer in time (still locked after login, a slow prompt), SahilBot made a new encryption key and saved keys became unreadable. Now it only makes a new key when the Keychain truly has none, and never overwrites one
A second Keychain item keeps a backup copy of the encryption key, so a deleted key is restored instead of replaced
If the Keychain is locked, Settings → Models & Keys says your keys are locked, not lost, with a Retry button. Don't re-enter them
A key you type while the Keychain is locked is no longer stored the old way that broke on the next update: you're asked to unlock and try again

sections.title: Medical research
items: PubMed searches can filter by evidence (guidelines, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, randomized trials) and date, and every result shows its evidence level
Retracted papers and expressions of concern are flagged
New sources: MeSH headings, Europe PMC (preprints marked as not peer reviewed, citation counts), open-access full text, FDA adverse event reports and MedlinePlus

Before a medical answer reaches you, SahilBot checks it: every cited PMID, DOI and trial ID must come from what it actually read, must exist in PubMed and must not be retracted. A clinical answer with no research behind it is sent back to check the evidence first
PubMed & medical sources is listed under Connect apps → Built in. No sign-in. An optional free NCBI key (Settings → Keys for tools) makes big research jobs faster

sections.title: Your vault, organized like Obsidian
items: Every memory is mirrored into the vault as linked notes: Shared/Memory has one note per category (About you, Preferences, People, Places, Projects…) with links to people and project notes
Your decisions get their own Decision log (Shared/Decisions), newest first and grouped by month, with what you chose over what
A bot's own memories go to that bot's area only. Text you write around the mirrored part is kept, every change can be undone, and secrets are never written
Vault is in the sidebar now (it was only in ⌘K)

sections.title: A copy of everything, in a separate place
items: The daily backup now includes your knowledge vault notes and a readable export of your memories and decisions
Set a recovery password (Settings → Privacy & Security → Backups) and each backup also holds your API keys, encrypted with it, so you can restore them on any Mac
Back up now, see the last backup, open both backup folders, or add an extra folder such as an external drive

sections.title: Bots that keep going
items: In a chat you're in, a bot that's still making progress keeps working past its usual step limit instead of stopping to ask you to say "continue" (your spending limit and the safety stops still apply)
Messages you send while a bot works reach it at its next step: it adjusts and keeps going, nothing stops
A routine that comes due while you're working with that bot waits its turn instead of being skipped, then runs on its own (it stops waiting if you pause or delete it)
After each routine, a dated line about what it did goes into the bot's work log, so its next run, its chats and your other bots build on it

Bots share what they learn: any bot, chat or helper can read what your other bots learned and did, labeled with the bot. Only trusted memories are shared (nothing worded from a web page or email), and each bot's own rules stay its own. Turn it off in Settings → Memory

sections.title: A steadier coding agent
items: If you edit a file while a bot is working on it, the bot can't overwrite your edit with its older copy: it's told to read the file again and add its change on top
A "done" claim is no longer second-guessed when the matching tool clearly ran ("published" after a publish tool), so connector tasks finish a step sooner
On SahilBot Server (Raspberry Pi, VMs), commands, tests and background jobs run in bash when zsh isn't installed (they failed before)
On the harness benchmark (the same scripted model through each harness), SahilBot now scores 100, against 72 for a Grok Build profile and 68 for Claude Code and Codex CLI profiles

sections.title: Auto, sharper on your kind of work
items: Clinical questions (doses, drug interactions, lab results, warning signs) go to the strongest model with the medical sources; a simple definition stays quick
Literature questions (meta-analyses, trials, guidelines, PMIDs, FDA labels) run as deep research
Handing work to Cursor, Codex or Claude Code runs as coding work and loads the Cursor, code and git tools; several agents at once or a repo-wide change gets the strongest model
Directions and "near me" are quick live lookups; comparing several places runs as research with maps; booking a table, room or flight is treated as a booking
Engineering calculations (deflection, stress, torque) are worked as math, not CAD
Measured on 40 new requests across these areas: the right kind of work went from 67.5% to 100%, and no task runs as a plain chat any more

sections.title: Maps and travel
items: Search places, get details, directions (driving, walking, cycling, transit), travel times between several places, and what's nearby (restaurants, sights, pharmacies, urgent care, EV charging and more)
Every answer has Google Maps links you can click. Without a key SahilBot uses OpenStreetMap; with a Google Maps key (Settings → Keys for tools) it uses Google's places and routes, including transit
Trip planning groups sights by area, checks travel times and gives one route link per day; new idea skills cover business, engineering, trips and local places
Maps & travel is listed under Connect apps → Built in

sections.title: SahilBot's own manual
items: When SahilBot isn't sure how a feature or tool works, it searches its manual before guessing or asking you

New pages: business (models, decks, research, recurring work), engineering (CAD, calculations, electronics, FRC, software) and coding agents (when to hand off to Cursor, writing the brief, reviewing the result)
The tools page now lists every tool SahilBot has

sections.title: Simpler to use
items: The sidebar has one New chat button, then Needs you, Vault, Artifacts and Brain, then your bots, projects and recent chats as quiet single rows
Home puts the message box first, with four suggestions and a small bot card below it
The browser and side-panel buttons only show in a chat, where they do something
Settings is one short list with no "More settings" fold. Phone & server pages only show once you've turned one on: SahilBot is a desktop app first
The "no model yet" notice is a clear card with Add a key and Retry buttons

sections.title: Bots you can talk to
items: In a voice chat, real work (research, a document, files, email, the browser) runs in the background in the bot's own chat, and the conversation keeps going
When the work finishes, the bot says the result in the next pause, if voice is still open. Ask follow-up questions about it right away
If the work needs your OK, the bot says so and the card shows on the voice screen. You tap to approve: a misheard "yes" never sends or buys anything
Voice is a bar at the top of the chat you're in, opened from the voice button in the message box: settings, transcript, mute and hang up
Pick a voice (hear each one first), the speaking speed and the language you speak
When you hang up, the conversation folds into one line named after what you talked about, with its length. Open it to read the transcript. What you said is remembered like anything you type
The voice bar lists what's running, what needs you and what's done
A new bot sets itself up with you in its chat
A new bot sets itself up with you in its chat, typed or by voice: it asks what you want done, suggests a name, writes its own instructions, and saves them when you agree
Spoken replies use cloud voices for speed and quality: ChatGPT's (OpenAI) or Grok's (xAI). Switch between them in the voice bar, even mid-conversation
Dictate with the microphone button: click to start and stop, or hold ⌘D and let go when you're done
First run ends with "Your first bot": how bots work in three short cards, then your first bot opens ready to set up

sections.title: Your iPhone, a server and your Mac
items: Run your bots around the clock on a small cloud server (DigitalOcean's 4 GB Droplet is about $24 a month) and use them from your iPhone as a Home Screen app

The server can use your Mac. At first it can only find and read your files. You can turn on Terminal, Messages, Mail, Notes, Calendar, the browser and the screen. Anything that changes something asks you first
Only the Mac you linked can take work from the server. Your Mac limits how fast the server can act and logs what it did
Your Mac connects out to the server, so nothing on your Mac is opened to the internet
Keep this Mac awake: while it's plugged in, your phone can always reach it (the display still turns off)
Setup steps are in the server guide (docs/server.md)
Keys, login items, mail and SahilBot's own data on your Mac are never reachable from the server, however a path is written
An action the server sends runs once, even if the connection hiccups; turning the link off stops it at once
Only your Mac can turn the link on or off

sections.title: Agent loop
items: When a tool fails and the agent starts to give up, it's sent to try another source or approach first, and it says plainly what blocked it if nothing works
A reply that says something was saved, sent or published when no tool ran gets challenged: it does it, or says it wasn't done
If a send times out, SahilBot won't repeat it (or ask you to approve a repeat) until the agent checks whether it already went through
After a code edit, the project's tests run right away on fast suites, so a wrong fix is caught before it's announced
A job that says it's still building gets a single wait instead of a tight polling loop
Project instructions in AGENTS.md (or CLAUDE.md / GROK.md) from your folder up to the repo root go into the agent's context, like Codex
If you set a limit ("under $200"), what the agent picks is checked against it, and it fixes a choice that's over
It reads every page of a paged result before answering, instead of stopping at page 1
A write that fails outright (bad input, no permission) no longer counts as "may have happened", so a corrected retry goes straight through
When the agent sees a better way or the obvious next step, it offers it as an idea card with "Do it". It never starts the idea on its own
It won't say "I can't access that" without trying the tools it has, and after a second failure it lists other ways and tries the best one
It reads curly apostrophes (I’ve, couldn’t) like straight ones, so its checks for false "done" claims and giving up always work
A reply the app sends back (it said it was done but wasn't, or gave up) is replaced by the next one instead of staying in the chat
Fewer false alarms on budgets ("under $2 million"), totals and fees, and on results that have no more pages

sections.title: Slides, documents and dashboards
items: Chart slides: a chart block on a slide draws in the deck's colors and exports to PowerPoint as a native chart you can edit
Share tables (Channel / Share) draw as donut charts on slides and dashboards
A deck check after the agent makes or exports a deck: too many points, long lines, missing or long titles get fixed before you see it
Documents show their word count and reading time next to the save state
Typing fast on a slide (Tab, Enter, then straight on) never drops a keystroke or undoes the step before
Tables on slides export to PowerPoint as real, editable tables
Pictures from the web are saved into your workspace, and WebP and iPhone (HEIC) pictures work in every export
Charts written as CSV work in documents too, not only in decks
If an export had to leave something out (a missing picture, text cut to fit), the bot tells you
Image captions are kept, italics no longer catch maths like 5 * 3, and long tables get a warning

sections.title: Privacy Gate, out of beta
items: Protect automatically (Settings → Hybrid compute): personal details get stand-ins for cloud models without pausing the chat, and a note says what was protected
Anything you mark "not personal" is remembered for every chat (never passwords, keys or account numbers), and Forget clears the list
See what the gate did today: requests checked, times it asked, details protected, and finds the model on your Mac cleared
PII-Tracer tests itself after the download, and restarts on its own if it stops mid-check

sections.title: Simpler Settings
items: Five main pages up front (General, Models, Connected apps, Privacy, Phone & server), with everything else under More settings. Search still finds every setting

sections.title: Fixes
items: API keys and other secrets are now sealed with SahilBot's own Keychain key, which stays the same across updates, so an update never asks you to enter them again

Keys saved before this update are moved over the first time they're read. If macOS asks whether "security" may use "SahilBot Safe Storage", enter your Mac password and choose Always Allow; your keys come back. If you choose Deny, they're kept, and you can allow it later

sections.title: Coming next
items: Accounts with Google sign-in, so several people can share one server privately
Your own checks that run before a bot says it's done (like Claude Code's hooks)
Picking up a long task exactly where it stopped after a crash or restart
Brand themes for decks and documents (your colors, font and logo), plus two-column and quote slides
Approving the server's actions on your Mac itself, for the most sensitive tools

title: Native decks, documents and dashboards, a smarter Auto, and Hybrid compute
highlights: Make slides, documents, dashboards and sheets right in SahilBot, edit them with your agent, and export to PowerPoint, Keynote/ODP, PDF, Word or images
Hybrid compute: personal details stay on your Mac while cloud models do the heavy lifting
Auto picks models from benchmark results for each kind of task, and pulls in a second model when two are better than one
Updates show their size, keep one copy of SahilBot installed, and back up your data in two places first

sections.title: Slides, documents and dashboards
items: New slide editor: click any text on a slide to type, add, duplicate and reorder slides, add big numbers, pictures and speaker notes, and present full screen
Slides look the same everywhere: the editor, Present, PDF, PNG and PowerPoint (pictures) are drawn by one renderer
Export a deck as editable PowerPoint, PowerPoint with exact fonts, OpenDocument (Keynote, LibreOffice, Google Slides), PDF or PNG images
New native dashboards: stat tiles, charts drawn from your tables, sections and notes
Artifacts page: start a Doc, Deck, Sheet or Dashboard in one click, and see the documents you're working on
Your agent now makes editable documents first and exports a PDF, Word or PowerPoint file when you want one
Open Word, PDF, PowerPoint, Excel and CSV files in the editor, change fonts and text, and save back to the original
Presenter view: your notes, the next slide and a timer while you present (press P)
Native sheets work out IF, SUMIF, VLOOKUP, XLOOKUP, text and date functions
Tables, numbered lists and checklists on a slide are kept when you edit it, and slides show their tables

sections.title: A more capable agent
items: Shows its plan as a live checklist and keeps it current as it works, so you can see where it is
Does what it says it will do, keeps going until the task is finished, and runs your tests until they pass after code changes
Says so plainly when it disagrees, and gives its reasons and the approach it would take
Remembers what you've said in your other chats with the same bot (only your own words), so answers fit you better
Plans and makes videos end to end: research, brief, shot list and the right platform at its best settings
Waits for you to sign in or type a code in the browser, then carries on by itself
Paste an API key or password into the chat and it goes straight into your vault

sections.title: Chat
items: Type / in the message box for commands: /new, /doc, /deck, /dashboard, /sheet, /research, /max, /plan, /voice, /artifacts, /settings, /whatsnew
Code in replies is syntax-colored; wide tables scroll and copy straight into Numbers or Excel
Inline citations like [1] link to their sources, numbered the same as the source chips
Press ↑ in an empty message box to edit your last message
Errors are in plain words with the next step, with the details a click away
If a message fails to send, your text comes back into the box

sections.title: Auto model routing
items: Each kind of task has its own model order, taken from published benchmarks: Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5 and GPT-6.2 Sol for daily work, GPT-6.2 Astra and Fable 5.2 for the hardest problems, Haiku 5.5 and GPT-6.1 Terra for quick ones, and GPT-6 Luna for a quick hello
Harder tasks get a stronger model, or two models working together when that's better
Context carries over perfectly when the model changes mid-chat

sections.title: Privacy and Hybrid compute
items: Hybrid compute on Macs with at least 32 GB of memory and 50 GB free (64 GB and 150 GB are best)
A local Privacy Gate (PII-Tracer) checks each cloud request on your Mac and asks before personal details leave it
